description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

editorialRead.readHeadline: NousResearch/hermes-agent is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: NousResearch/hermes-agent leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 27 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 27 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: NousResearch/hermes-agent — 71 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 168.7 below its current daily pace, with 63 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 79 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
Kilo-Org/kilocode — No same-day commit after 202 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Audit workflow cache keys before pinning agents to review worktrees
dailyInsight.insight: Qwen Code's merged workflow change treats an existing linked worktree as part of a subagent dispatch and includes that directory in the workflow journal identity. Builders who resume or cache workflow-agent work across review branches should audit whether their own harness records the workspace identity, rather than assuming the prompt alone identifies what was inspected.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The public commit adds `workingDir` for workflow agents, routes a pinned agent away from a path that would leave it on the parent configuration, validates the directory as a registered linked worktree of the same repository, and adds `workingDir` to canonicalized journal options. The documentation distinguishes this caller-owned pin from fresh worktree isolation and rejects the conflicting pair in workflows.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A reusable answer is unsafe when the same task text can be asked against two different uncommitted trees. The bounded action is an audit of dispatch identity and cache behavior, not a claim that a particular Qwen Code release or every agent workflow has a wrong-tree defect.

actions.audience: Builder or operator maintaining a resumable workflow-agent harness
actions.label: Check that workspace identity participates in resume and cache keys
actions.instruction: In a disposable repository with two linked worktrees that differ in one harmless fixture, run the same read-only review prompt once per tree. Inspect only redacted local diagnostics to confirm that the second run cannot reuse the first tree's answer. If the harness supports a caller-owned worktree option, also verify that it rejects a contradictory request to create a separate isolated worktree. Do not run the test against a production branch or sensitive checkout.
actions.effort: 30–60 minutes for a disposable two-worktree reproduction and cache-key inspection

receipts.title: feat(core): let a workflow agent pin a directory and outlive the default bounds (#8972)
receipts.supports: Shows the merged workflow implementation, registered-linked-worktree validation, fast-path avoidance, and journal-key treatment for `workingDir`.

receipts.title: Qwen Code sub-agent working-directory documentation at commit 2bbaafbf2
receipts.supports: Shows the documented distinction between caller-owned linked worktrees and workflow isolation, including the workflow conflict rule.

confidence.basis: A fresh public commit, its implementation description, and revision-pinned documentation agree on a narrowly scoped workflow identity contract. The action asks readers to test their own cache behavior rather than infer release or adoption status.

dailyInsight.limitation: The receipts are merged source and documentation. They do not establish that the change is released, that a wrong-tree incident occurred, or that another workflow system uses the same worktree and resume semantics.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw the call if a public reproduction shows that Qwen Code's workflow resume key excludes the bound worktree after this change, or if its documented workflow path safely canonicalizes an equivalent caller-owned tree without recording the directory in dispatch identity.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a release note or a public issue that runs the workflow path against two real linked review worktrees and documents the resulting cache or resume behavior.
